records.name: Cradle of Liberty Council, Scouting America
records.summary: The Scouting America council for Philadelphia, Montgomery and Delaware Counties. It runs Cub Scouts, Scouts BSA, Venturing, Sea Scouts and Exploring through local units, and it checks the adults who lead them first.
records.what_you_do: Youth join a local unit by age: Cub Scouts for ages 5 to 10, Scouts BSA for ages 11 to 17, Venturing and Sea Scouts for ages 14 to 20, and Exploring for ages 10 to 20. Adults can take unit roles such as Scoutmaster, Cubmaster or committee member, after youth safety training and Pennsylvania clearances, with an online application at beascout.org that carries a fee.

schedule.text: Each unit sets its own meeting times, and the council's pages do not list them.

locations.label: Service Center
locations.address: 901 East 8th Ave, Suite 103, King of Prussia, PA 19406

cost.text: The council pages do not state a youth membership fee. Adult volunteer applications carry a fee paid at registration.

first_step.how: Find a program near you at beascout.scouting.org, or call the service center at 610-688-6900 to ask which unit is closest.
first_step.basis: Families get a clear route to a unit and a phone line to ask. Adult leaders must finish training and Pennsylvania clearances before they start, so they cannot see the role first.

records.notes: Clearances named on the council's pages: Pennsylvania State Police criminal record check, Child Abuse History Clearance, and an FBI fingerprint check for adults who lived in Pennsylvania under 10 years; longer residents file a disclosure statement instead. The council's page says the state checks are free for most volunteers and last five years. The only fee quoted for fingerprints is from 2022 and was not used. The council's dated items have no year (Labor Day closure, Celebration of Scouting, Cub Scout Fall Fest), so status is probably_active. Individual packs, troops and crews are not listed here; see leads_only.

records.name: Girl Scouts of Eastern Pennsylvania
records.summary: The Girl Scout council for Philadelphia and eight nearby counties. Girls join troops, and adults lead a troop, help one, or take council roles such as committee member or awards mentor.
records.what_you_do: Girls join a troop, which meets at times and places its leaders set. Adults can start a troop, help an existing troop with skills, the cookie program or chaperoning, share first aid or outdoor skills, join a council committee, or mentor girls working toward the Silver and Gold Awards. Adult volunteers must be 18 or older.

schedule.text: Each troop sets its own meeting times and place, so ask the troop leader. The council's home page lists events by date.

cost.text: The council lists a membership fee, but the pages read do not state an amount.

first_step.how: Fill in the volunteer interest form on gsep.org, or call 215-564-2030 to ask about a troop near you.
first_step.basis: Anyone can ask through the public interest form, and the council says it will follow up. It does not describe a beginner program or a first visit, so you cannot see a troop before you join.

records.notes: The council's own clearances page is linked but its wording was not read, so requirements.act153_clearances is left out. The phone number and office address come from a PA 211 listing, not the council site. The council's home page footer reads 2016 to 2023 (not used as evidence); the only dated item is an upcoming Sunday Oct 11 pop-up event in North Wales, with the year taken from the event link. Philadelphia service unit names and meeting areas were not found; see leads_only.

records.name: Big Brothers Big Sisters Independence Region
records.summary: A mentoring agency for Philadelphia and six nearby counties in Pennsylvania and New Jersey. Adult volunteers, called Bigs, spend regular time with one child through a one-to-one mentoring program.
records.what_you_do: Bigs take part in one-to-one mentoring through one of several programs: community-based mentoring, site-based mentoring, Beyond School Walls, an LGBTQ+ program, or POWER Up. A visit lasts about two hours, at least twice a month. Bigs must be 21 or older.

schedule.text: Visits last about two hours, at least twice a month, for a commitment of a year or more. The site gives both 18 months and one year, so ask for the exact term.

cost.text: The site does not state a cost for becoming a Big.

first_step.how: Fill in the short inquiry form on the Be a Big page, then book the virtual interview with a staff member.
first_step.basis: The steps are clear (inquiry, virtual interview, application with background checks, then a match), but a person cannot see the program before the interview and application.

records.notes: Bigs must be 21 or older, must live in the service area (Philadelphia, Chester, Montgomery, Delaware, Camden, Burlington or Gloucester County), and must have a car if they live outside Philadelphia. The site says background checks but does not name Pennsylvania clearances, so act153_clearances is left out. Ages of the children served are not stated on the pages read. The only dated item is a future Big Futures Breakfast (April 7, 2027), so status is probably_active, not active. The domain bbbsi.org returned an unrelated gambling page and was not used.

records.name: Boys and Girls Clubs of Philadelphia
records.summary: A youth club organization in Philadelphia neighborhoods, offering preschool, after-school and teen programs at clubhouses such as Bridesburg, Northeast Frankford, Germantown and Wissahickon.
records.what_you_do: Children take part in after-school, preschool and teen activities at a neighborhood clubhouse. The homepage does not say how a child signs up, what membership costs, or how adults volunteer.

schedule.text: After-school, preschool and teen programs at neighborhood clubhouses. The homepage does not give days or hours.

locations.label: Henry Reed Hatfield Outdoor Recreation Complex (Nicetown)

cost.text: The homepage does not say what membership costs.

first_step.how: Call the office at (215) 735-8818 or email admin@bgcphila.org to ask which club is nearest and how a child signs up.
first_step.basis: The homepage gives no sign-up steps, so the only way in that is published is a phone call or an email to the office.

records.notes: The homepage gives no ages served, sign-up steps, membership cost, clubhouse addresses or volunteer process. The newest dated item is a June 2026 call for renovation bids at the Northeast Frankford Club (bids due Aug 24, 2026), which shows the organization is active but is not a program event. Next step: ask the office for club addresses and the volunteer process.

records.name: Police Athletic League of Philadelphia
records.summary: A youth development group with free sports, learning, character-building and cultural programs for kids ages 6 to 18. Its 15 community sites each have an on-duty police officer, and 3 school sites run during the school year.
records.what_you_do: Kids take part in free sports, learning and character programs at a site near them. Adults 18 and older can volunteer for at least 2 hours per event, and the Programs Department reviews each volunteer request first.

schedule.text: Free programs at 15 community sites and 3 school sites during the school year. Hours and site addresses are not on the homepage.

cost.text: The PAL site says all of its programs are free.

first_step.how: Call PAL headquarters at (215) 291-9000 and ask which community site is closest to you.
first_step.basis: Programs are free and open to kids 6 to 18, but the site does not list centers or sign-up steps, so the way in is a phone call.

records.notes: The volunteer page says clearances will be required for ongoing youth-facing roles but does not name them, so requirements.act153_clearances and background_check are left out. Its 2026 events (awards gala, PAL Day at City Hall, golf classic) have no dates, so status is probably_active. The court-ordered and school service contacts on the site are named staff; they are not recorded here, and people should go through the main line.

records.name: Philadelphia County 4-H (Penn State Extension)
records.summary: The Philadelphia County branch of Pennsylvania 4-H, run by Penn State Extension. Young people join project clubs in areas such as STEM, animal science, civic engagement and healthy living.
records.what_you_do: Members choose a project club, meet with it on a regular schedule, and pay a fee for educational materials. Adults help run clubs as screened volunteers, and a new club needs at least two screened adult volunteers.

schedule.text: Each club sets its own meeting times, so the county office can say which clubs meet near you. The office is staffed Monday to Friday, 9 am to 5 pm, with a break from 1 to 2 pm, so call ahead.

cost.text: Members pay a fee for educational materials. The amount is not on the page and varies by county and project, and financial help is available.

first_step.how: Call 215-471-2200 or email PhiladelphiaExt@psu.edu, or register through 4-H's ZSuite system at 4h.zsuite.org.
first_step.basis: Anyone from age 5 to 18 can join and the county explains club options by phone or email, though it does not describe a beginner program.

records.notes: The clubs page lists project areas only and names no individual clubs; ask the county office for the club list. The enrollment steps for new adult volunteers are on a separate page (Enrolling in 4-H as a New Volunteer) that was not read, so the screening type and any Pennsylvania clearances are unknown and left out. The page's only date is the copyright footer, so status is probably_active.

notes: Budget: all 8 WebSearch calls used (hard cap reached, no further searching). 24 WebFetch calls, including failures. Result: 6 publish, 0 hide. Not written as records (see leads_only): Little League districts, EPYSA member clubs, the Philadelphia Parks and Recreation soccer league, CYO, individual Scouting units and Girl Scout service units.
